repeated.title: Is a customer required at creation; what create takes

1.1.title: Create: which inputs besides name and address, and is customer required
behaviours: Create requires name and address only; customer reference is optional and may be set later by 'correct a project'
Create also requires a customer reference (R0-01 lists it as identity) and refuses a project without one
1.1.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel and onboard_object, whose create calls without a customer either succeed or are refused; PresuPro/Client Portal reading an empty customer in context

2.5.title: Is a customer required at creation
behaviours: Create a project without a customer and let it be set later by 'correct a project'
Refuse a project without a customer, since R0-01 lists the customer reference as part of identity and context always carries 'customer'
2.5.who_notices: Staff onboarding a project before the customer is known; consumers reading an empty customer in context

3.3.title: Inputs of create: is the customer required
behaviours: A project can be created without a customer and gets one later through correct.
A project without a customer is refused, like one missing a name or address.
3.3.who_notices: Staff and Cabinet Kernel creating a project before the customer is known; consumers reading a context with no customer.

repeated.title: What correcting a project may change (blank, partial)

1.2.title: Correct: are blank name/address refused as on create
1.2.quote: the project with the new name, address or customer
behaviours: Correction applies the same rule as create and refuses an empty name or address
Correction accepts any supplied value, so a project can end up with an empty name or address
1.2.who_notices: Staff in the frontend; consumers whose context snapshot then carries an empty display name or address

3.4.title: Correct may or may not blank a field or change several at once
3.4.quote: | correct a project | staff | the project with the new name, address or customer | unknown id refused; correcting an archived project: OQ-07 |
behaviours: Correct refuses an empty name or address, the same rule as create, and may change any subset of fields together.
Correct changes exactly one of the three fields per call and accepts whatever value it is given, empty values included.
3.4.who_notices: Staff in the frontend, and consumers that later read a project with an empty name or address.

repeated.title: Listing rooms of an unknown project

1.3.title: List rooms on an unknown project: empty list or not found
1.3.quote: | list rooms | staff, consumer service | the project's rooms in a declared order | — |
behaviours: Unknown project id returns an empty room list (no failure, as the table says)
Unknown project id is refused as not found, like 'list artifacts' ('unknown project') and 'read a project'
1.3.who_notices: Consumer services that mistype a project id and either see 'no rooms' or an error

2.6.title: 'List rooms' for an unknown project has no stated failure
2.6.quote: | list rooms | staff, consumer service | the project's rooms in a declared order | — |
behaviours: Answer an empty list for an unknown project id
Refuse an unknown project as not found, like every other per-project action
2.6.who_notices: Consumer services that rely on the list to detect a mistyped project id

3.10.title: List rooms of an unknown project
3.10.quote: | list rooms | staff, consumer service | the project's rooms in a declared order | — |
behaviours: Listing rooms of an unknown project is refused as not found, like read a project.
Listing rooms of an unknown project returns an empty list.
3.10.who_notices: Consumers that cannot tell a project without rooms from a wrong project id.

repeated.title: A room's inputs and stored facts are unnamed

1.4.title: What a room is: its input and identity are unnamed
1.4.quote: | add a room | staff, consumer service | the room in the project |
behaviours: A room is a name only; two rooms with the same name in one project are allowed
A room has a name unique within the project and a duplicate is refused
1.4.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel / operator adding rooms on replay; downstream services launched with a room_id

3.11.title: The inputs and stored facts of a room are not named
3.11.quote: | add a room | staff, consumer service | the room in the project |
behaviours: A room is just a name inside a project, and duplicate names are allowed.
A room carries more facts (kind, area, a unique label inside the project), and adding a duplicate is refused.
3.11.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel and staff adding rooms; downstream services that launch with room_id.

repeated.title: 'Archived only when asked': alongside active or alone

1.5.title: 'Archived only when asked': included alongside active, or archived alone
1.5.quote: the projects, archived only when asked
behaviours: Asking adds archived projects to the active ones (all projects)
Asking returns only archived projects
1.5.who_notices: Staff browsing the archive in the frontend; any consumer that counts projects

2.7.title: 'Archived only when asked': included alongside active, or alone
2.7.quote: the projects, archived only when asked
behaviours: When asked, return active and archived projects together
When asked, return only archived projects (a separate archived listing)
2.7.who_notices: Staff in the Registry frontend looking for an archived project; consumers paging projects

repeated.title: Does the artifact list include superseded versions; how is history read

1.6.title: Artifact history: does 'list artifacts' include superseded versions
1.6.quote: Publishing a new version of a type supersedes the previous one; the history stays readable.
behaviours: 'list artifacts' returns every version, published and superseded
'list artifacts' returns only published pointers, and history is readable some other way (by id) that no action in the table carries
1.6.who_notices: Consumer services and staff looking for an older estimate version

2.8.title: Does the artifact list include superseded versions, and how is history read
2.8.quote: Publishing a new version of a type supersedes the previous one; the history stays readable.
behaviours: 'list artifacts' returns every version including superseded ones, which is how history is readable
'list artifacts' returns only published pointers, and history is reachable only by reading a specific version, an action no row of the table carries
2.8.who_notices: Consumer services that show estimate history or want only the current documents

3.8.title: Does list artifacts include superseded versions
behaviours: List artifacts returns every version, superseded ones included, and that list is the history.
List artifacts returns published pointers only; history needs some other filter or action, and the text names none.
3.8.who_notices: Consumers and staff looking for an earlier estimate version.

1.7.title: Scope of supersession: per project, per room, or per producer
1.7.quote: the previous published version of that type becomes `superseded`
behaviours: Supersession is per (project, type): a new estimate for any room supersedes the project's previous one
Supersession is per (project, room, type) or per (project, type, owner service), so several published pointers of one type coexist in a project
1.7.who_notices: Consumers calling 'read the latest of a type', who get one pointer or must choose among several; producers publishing room-level documents (launch context carries room_id)

2.10.title: Supersession scope: per project and type, or also per owner
2.10.unit: Primary actions / publish an artifact pointer
2.10.quote: the previous published version of that type becomes `superseded`
behaviours: Supersede the previous published pointer of the same type in the same project regardless of owner
Supersede only the caller-owner's previous pointer of that type, so two owners publishing the same type keep two published pointers (relevant if OQ-03 lets a type have several owners)
2.10.who_notices: Consumers calling 'read the latest of a type' and getting one or another owner's document

repeated.title: No action withdraws an artifact pointer

1.9.title: No action to withdraw a pointer whose artifact the owner deleted
behaviours: Pointers can only be superseded; a pointer to a deleted estimate stays 'published' and dangles
A producer can withdraw/revoke its pointer, leaving no published artifact of that type (or the previous one restored)
1.9.who_notices: Consumers following the latest pointer to a document that no longer exists; the producer service that deleted it

3.9.title: No action withdraws an artifact pointer
behaviours: A published pointer stays published until a newer version supersedes it, even when the producer has deleted or withdrawn its document.
A producer can retract or withdraw its pointer, so latest of a type then answers nothing or the previous version.
3.9.who_notices: Consumers following a latest pointer to a document the producer has already deleted.

1.11.title: What changes the 'updated' time in the pinned context
behaviours: updated changes only on correct and archive of the project itself
updated also changes when a room is added or an artifact pointer is published
1.11.who_notices: Consumers that refresh their snapshot when updated moves; Client Portal showing 'last updated'

2.15.title: What moves the 'updated' time
2.15.unit: Primary actions / read a project context
2.15.quote: id, display name, status, address, customer, created and updated times
behaviours: Only correct and archive change the updated time
Adding a room or publishing an artifact also changes the project's updated time
2.15.who_notices: Consumers using the updated time to decide whether their snapshot is stale

3.5.title: What changes the updated time
behaviours: Updated time moves only when name, address, customer or status changes.
Updated time also moves when a room is added or an artifact is published for the project.
3.5.who_notices: Consumers that compare the snapshot time to decide whether their copy is stale.

repeated.title: Are the frontend and onboard_object inside the product

1.12.title: Is onboard_object inside the product boundary
1.12.quote: through the Registry frontend or an operator script (`onboard_object`)
behaviours: onboard_object is part of the re-authored Registry and is specified and rebuilt with it
onboard_object is an external caller of the HTTP API that the Registry does not own and only must not break (OQ-08)
1.12.who_notices: The owner/operator running onboarding after the re-authoring

2.13.title: Are the frontend and onboard_object inside the product boundary
2.13.quote: through the Registry frontend or an operator script (`onboard_object`)
behaviours: Re-author the frontend and onboard_object as part of Registry, so their behaviour is specified here
Specify only the HTTP API; the frontend and script are external clients that must adapt
2.13.who_notices: Staff using the frontend/script; whoever must change them under OQ-08

3.12.title: Is the frontend part of the product
3.12.quote:
the Registry frontend from its own origin; CORS admits exactly
  that origin.
behaviours: The frontend is in scope: it is built and shipped with Registry, and its origin is fixed by the product.
The frontend is an external client: Registry is only the HTTP API, and the admitted origin is per-instance configuration.
3.12.who_notices: Staff using the frontend, and the operator deploying a new instance.

1.13.title: 'Nothing is deleted' vs personal data if OQ-01 brings it here
1.13.quote: the project, status `archived`; nothing is deleted (V1-7)
behaviours: Customer contact data stays forever with the archived project, never erased
Contact data can be erased or corrected on request while the project record is kept, needing an action no promise carries
1.13.who_notices: The customer exercising data-protection rights; the owner answering for it

3.13.title: Never deleting conflicts with erasing personal data
behaviours: Customer contact data, if OQ-01 brings it here, can never be erased: archive keeps everything.
Contact data can be erased or anonymised on request, which needs an action that no promise carries and an exception to R0-03.
3.13.who_notices: The customer asking to be forgotten, and the owner answering a data-protection request.

repeated.title: Who publishes artifacts: actors vs producer services

2.3.title: Which actors publish artifacts contradicts between sections
2.3.quote: Cabinet Kernel and the operator also create projects and rooms and publish artifacts.
behaviours: Treat Cabinet Kernel and the operator as producer services for some artifact types and admit their publishes
Admit publishes only from the producer list ('today: PresuPro estimates; planners by name only') and refuse Kernel/operator publishes as unknown owner
2.3.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel and the operator when their publish is refused or accepted

3.1.title: Operator and Cabinet Kernel publish artifacts but are not producer services
3.1.quote:
Cabinet Kernel
  and the operator also create projects and rooms and publish artifacts.
behaviours: Publish accepts any caller that names a known owner, so Cabinet Kernel and the operator publish as if they were producers.
Publish accepts only the producer services listed under Producer services (PresuPro, planners), so a Kernel or operator publish is refused as an unknown owner.
3.1.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel and the operator running onboard_object, when their publish is accepted or refused.

repeated.title: Which consumer services may create projects and rooms

2.4.title: Which consumer services may create projects and rooms
2.4.unit: Primary actions / create a project, add a room
2.4.quote: | create a project | staff, consumer service |
behaviours: Any consumer service (PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet Web mirror) may create projects and rooms
Only Cabinet Kernel and the operator may, as the Actors section says; other consumers are read-only
2.4.who_notices: The owner, when Client Portal or PresuPro creates stray projects; consumer authors

3.2.title: Which consumer services may create projects and rooms
3.2.quote: | create a project | staff, consumer service |
behaviours: Every consumer service (PresuPro, Client Portal, the Cabinet Web mirror included) may create projects and add rooms.
Only Cabinet Kernel and the operator may create; the other consumers only validate and read, as the actor list says.
3.2.who_notices: Owner, when PresuPro or Client Portal creates projects or rooms that staff did not expect.

repeated.title: Consumers never learn of a correction or archive

2.14.title: Stale snapshots after a correction: no change signal
2.14.quote: reads that identity as a snapshot; none of them writes it back (V1-2).
behaviours: Registry only answers reads; a consumer keeps the old name/address/customer until it reads again on its own
Registry notifies or exposes changes (event, changed-since list) so consumers refresh snapshots
2.14.who_notices: Client Portal / PresuPro users seeing an old address or customer after staff corrected it

3.6.title: Consumers never learn about a correction or an archive
3.6.quote:
Consumers snapshot it at read time and never write
it back.
behaviours: Registry notifies nobody; a consumer keeps its stale snapshot until it reads again on its own schedule.
Registry tells consumers about a correction or an archive (an event or callback) so they can refresh their snapshot.
3.6.who_notices: Client Portal and PresuPro users who still see the old name or address after staff corrected it.

single.title: Replay of an artifact publish
single.quote: the new version, `published`; the previous published version of that type becomes `superseded`
behaviours: An identical second publish (same uri/payload_ref) creates another version and supersedes the first
An identical second publish returns the existing version unchanged
single.who_notices: PresuPro retrying after a timeout; consumers seeing duplicate history entries

single.title: 'display name' in the pinned context vs 'name' in identity
single.quote: id, display name, status, address, customer, created and updated times
behaviours: display name is the project's name, unchanged
display name is derived (e.g. name plus address or customer) and differs from name
single.who_notices: PresuPro and Client Portal, which pin the context fields and show the value to users

single.title: Option (a) of OQ-01 needs customer actions no promise carries
single.quote: a Customer record in Registry, with `customer_ref` becoming its identity
behaviours: Customers are created/corrected implicitly through 'create/correct a project' with inline contact data
Customers are a separate record with their own create/read/correct actions, shared by several projects of one customer
single.who_notices: Staff entering a returning customer's second project; the agent reading the phone for the WhatsApp link

single.title: Role restrictions in the 'who' column cannot be told apart without authentication
single.quote: | correct a project | staff | the project with the new name, address or customer |
behaviours: Treat 'who' as documentation only: any caller on loopback/private network may correct and archive projects, because nothing distinguishes staff from a consumer service while OQ-04 is open
Invent a caller distinction now (header, separate port, frontend-only route) so that only 'staff' can correct/archive and consumer services are refused
single.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel / consumer service authors (whether their correct/archive calls succeed) and the owner reviewing who changed a project

single.title: Producer identity ('owner') is self-declared and unverifiable
single.unit: Primary actions / publish an artifact pointer
single.quote: unknown or archived project, unknown type or owner refused (OQ-03)
behaviours: Accept whatever owner name the caller states and check it only against the vocabulary, so any service can publish (and supersede) a pointer in another service's name
Bind the owner to the calling service (by network origin or credential) and refuse a publish whose declared owner is not the caller
single.who_notices: PresuPro, whose latest estimate pointer could be superseded by another caller; Client Portal reading the latest artifact

single.title: Failure of 'list artifacts' when nothing is published
single.unit: Primary actions / list artifacts / read the latest of a type
single.quote: unknown project; no published artifact of that type
behaviours: Both list and read-latest refuse when no published artifact of the type exists
Listing answers an empty list; only 'read the latest of a type' refuses
single.who_notices: Client Portal / Cabinet consumers rendering a project with no documents yet

single.title: R0-04 defers to OQ-08, but OQ-08 does not cover validate/context
single.quote: keeps both answers field for field unless the owner decides otherwise under OQ-08.
behaviours: Freeze validate and context unconditionally, since OQ-08 only asks about bare-array lists and the nested project id
Treat validate/context shapes as open under OQ-08 and reshape them with the rest of the wire
single.who_notices: PresuPro and Client Portal, which pin those field names

single.title: Which consumers' reads are contracts besides PresuPro and Client Portal
single.quote: PresuPro and Client Portal read `validate` and `context` and pin their field names.
behaviours: Only those two answers for those two consumers are frozen; Cabinet Kernel and the Cabinet Web mirror may be broken
Every answer any listed consumer reads (Kernel, Web mirror, frontend, onboard_object) is held stable
single.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel and Cabinet Web mirror maintainers after a re-authored release

single.title: Launch context has no action that produces it
single.quote: Registry gives the launch context (`project_id`, optional `room_id`) and nothing else (V1-3).
behaviours: 'Launch context' is just the ids already returned by read/context; no extra action exists
A separate action returns a launch context (e.g. validates a room belongs to the project) that no row of the table carries
single.who_notices: Downstream services launched with a room_id from another project

single.title: 'Project card' content is unnamed
single.quote: the project card (any status, V1-7) and its rooms
behaviours: The card holds the same facts as the context answer plus rooms
The card carries further stored facts (e.g. artifacts, archive time, customer details) that the context does not
single.who_notices: Staff in the frontend and consumers choosing between read and context

single.title: Which instance a consumer talks to, and why several exist
single.quote: An instance holds its own store. Two instances share nothing
behaviours: One instance per host/environment; each consumer is configured with exactly one Registry
Consumers may reach several instances and must tell projects apart across them, which the document leaves to OQ-02 only
single.who_notices: Operators deploying Registry and consumers resolving a project id

single.title: No action reads an artifact by id
single.quote:
An archived project, its rooms and its artifacts stay
readable by id
behaviours: An artifact read-by-id action exists, as R0-03 implies, even though the table does not list it.
Artifacts are reachable only through list artifacts or latest of a type, so 'readable by id' means only the project id.
single.who_notices: A consumer holding an artifact id that it needs to resolve back to its pointer.
